scenes.line1: How do you track evolving data?
scenes.say: When your data changes over time, how do you keep track of every version? Can SQL really help you keep history straight?

scenes.label: SCD
scenes.sub: Slowly Changing Dimensions record changes over time.
scenes.say: Slowly Changing Dimensions are a way to capture how your data shifts, so you always know what changed and when.
MERGE and upsert statements let you update and add records in one step. This is key for tracking changes efficiently.

scenes.code:
MERGE INTO customers t
USING updates s ON t.id = s.id
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET t.name = s.name
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (id, name)
VALUES (s.id, s.name);
scenes.say: Here's a real-world example. MERGE lets you update names if the customer exists, or add them if they're new—all in one go.

scenes.question: How do you preserve history with SCD?
scenes.right: Close out old records and insert a new row with the updated values and a new effective date. This keeps the full history.
scenes.say: Interviewers want to see you preserve history. Don't just overwrite data—make sure you keep every version.
